questions.prompt: A chat component must connect whenever roomId changes. Where should connection synchronization live?

choices.text: Inside render, so every calculation opens another connection.
Only in a click handler, even when roomId changes externally.
In an Effect whose setup connects and cleanup disconnects.
In a module variable shared by every chat component instance.

questions.explanation: An Effect synchronizes the connection with current inputs. Render must not open external connections.

questions.prompt: The total price is fully determined by current item props. Which approach avoids unnecessary synchronization?

choices.text: Store every intermediate total in an Effect with no dependencies.
Calculate the derived total during rendering from current inputs.
Open a subscription that changes props after every render.
Mutate the supplied item array so the new total becomes state.

questions.explanation: A pure derived value needs no external-system synchronization. Storing it through an Effect adds redundant state.

sources.title: Synchronizing with Effects
sources.claim: Effects synchronize external systems rather than being needed for every calculation derived from existing state.

questions.prompt: An Effect reads roomId but declares []. What is the central bug if roomId changes?

choices.text: It always reconnects twice on every roomId change in production.
React mutates the dependency list automatically to insert roomId.
It retains the captured roomId and does not resynchronize for the change.
An empty dependency list makes the Effect execute on every render.

questions.explanation: Dependencies declare the reactive values needed for resynchronization. Omitting one creates stale synchronization.

questions.prompt: An Effect depends on a fresh options object created on every render. Why does unrelated state reconnect it?

choices.text: The object identity differs under Object.is on each render.
The dependency is deeply equal, so only an unrelated state bug could reconnect.
React compares object properties recursively before each Effect.
A dependency array always forces reconnecting after every render.

questions.explanation: Fresh objects are unequal references. Move construction inside the Effect or depend on relevant stable values.

questions.prompt: The room changes from A to B. Which lifecycle order avoids retaining both connections?

choices.text: Clean up A, then run setup using the current room B value.
Keep A connected because cleanup runs only on component removal.
Disconnect B before connecting A, then retain A until unmount.
Connect B, render A again, then skip A cleanup until unmount.

questions.explanation: Changed dependencies trigger old cleanup before new setup. Cleanup is not limited to unmount.

questions.prompt: Search A starts, then B starts. B finishes first. What prevents A later overwriting B?

choices.text: Call the setter unconditionally for both response callbacks.
Ignore the obsolete response using cleanup-linked request state.
Assume HTTP responses always complete in request-start order.
Remove the search term dependency so only A can ever run.

questions.explanation: The documented fetch pattern marks an old Effect ignored during cleanup, so only the current request applies results.

questions.prompt: Which uses belong in external-system Effects? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Compute a sum of existing props without any external system.
Send a purchase for every render whether a user clicked or not.
Connect to a third-party widget that lives outside React.
Subscribe to browser events and remove that subscription later.
Synchronize a network connection with the selected room.

questions.explanation: A: Incorrect: a pure derived calculation can run during render. B: Incorrect: an interaction-specific purchase belongs to its event. C: Correct: external widgets can require synchronization. D: Correct: event subscriptions are external synchronization. E: Correct: connection state must follow the room input.

sources.title: Synchronizing with Effects
sources.claim: Effects synchronize external APIs such as events, connections and widgets; interaction-specific actions belong in event handlers.

questions.prompt: Which dependency claims are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Omitting a used value makes the closure automatically read its latest value.
React compares dependencies by recursively checking nested object fields.
Changing a used dependency can trigger cleanup and setup again.
Reactive values used by setup must be represented as dependencies.
Object.is compares dependencies between successive renders.

questions.explanation: A: Incorrect: the closure retains its render values. B: Incorrect: comparison uses Object.is, not deep equality. C: Correct: changed inputs require resynchronization. D: Correct: dependencies reflect the setup reactive inputs. E: Correct: this is the documented comparison.

questions.prompt: Which lifecycle claims hold for a well-formed subscription Effect? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Cleanup occurs only after the browser tab is permanently closed.
Cleanup removes the subscription established by its setup.
Changed dependencies run old cleanup before the new setup.
Setup must always run exactly once even in development Strict Mode.
Development may exercise setup and cleanup to detect missing cleanup.

questions.explanation: A: Incorrect: cleanup also runs on changes and unmount. B: Correct: cleanup should undo setup. C: Correct: the old external state is removed first. D: Incorrect: development checks can exercise an extra cycle. E: Correct: the extra cycle exposes missing reversibility.

questions.prompt: Which claims help handle stale fetch results? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Cleanup can mark the previous Effect response as obsolete.
Apply a response only while its associated request is current.
Network response order always matches request-start order.
Ignoring an old response guarantees the server never processed its request.
A cleanup flag can prevent an obsolete response from replacing newer UI data.

questions.explanation: A: Correct: the documented pattern uses an ignore flag. B: Correct: current-request ownership avoids stale UI writes. C: Incorrect: responses can arrive in any order. D: Incorrect: ignoring UI application is not server cancellation. E: Correct: this addresses out-of-order completion.
